header:
Unlike most covalent compounds, whose structures can be described using 2c-2e bonds, polyhedral clusters are often electron-deficient systems and require multicenter bonding models.
Wade's rules, more generally known as the polyhedral skeletal electron pair theory (PSEPT), are an important tool for understanding cluster structures. Let $n$ denote the number of atoms or isolobal fragments that form the cluster framework. Subtracting the electrons used in terminal two-center two-electron bonds, nonskeletal lone pairs, and the internal bonding of ligands from the total valence-electron count gives the number of skeletal electrons. Skeletal electron-pair counts of $n+1$, $n+2$, $n+3$, and $n+4$ correspond, respectively, to closo, nido, arachno, and hypho structures. A closo cluster is a complete triangulated polyhedron with $n$ vertices, whereas nido, arachno, and hypho clusters may be regarded as the corresponding closo parent polyhedron with one, two, or three vertices removed, respectively. For example, in $B_5H_9$, 5 BH fragments contribute 10 electrons and 4 additional hydrogen atoms contribute another 4, giving 14 skeletal electrons or 7 skeletal electron pairs. Since the skeletal electron-pair count is $n+2$, the cluster is nido.
This problem uses low-valent clusters of Group 13 metals (Al, Ga, In, and Tl) to examine cluster synthesis, structure, bonding, and reactivity.

subquestions.text_open: 5.1 $B_4Cl_4$ and $B_4(t\text{-}Bu)_4$ have tetrahedral cores, whereas the acetamido-substituted boron compound $B_4(NHAc)_4$ adopts a butterfly-shaped cyclic structure. Explain why.

5.2 Write equations for the following reactions.
5.2.1 $AlCl\cdot x\,Et_2O$ ($x>1$) reacts with $MgCp^*_2$ at low temperature in toluene/diethyl ether to form $Al_4Cp^*_4$.
5.2.2 $GaI$ reacts with $Li(THF)_3Ge(SiMe_3)_3$ in toluene to form $[GaGe(SiMe_3)_3]_4$.

5.4 Tetrahedral clusters not only have unusual structures but also show diverse oxidation chemistry, giving different products under different conditions. Draw the structures of products A, B, D, and E below. 5.4.1 Oxidation of [GaSi(t-Bu)_3]_4 with oxygen gives cubic cluster A = [OGaSi(t-Bu)_3]_4.

5.4.2 Further hydrolysis of A gives product B, which contains only one ring and has only one chemical environment for its Ga atoms. Write the SMILES string for B. If necessary, describe its detailed structure in no more than 50 words. Multiple reasonable structures may be possible; writing any one reasonable SMILES string is sufficient.

5.4.3 Oxidation of $C = [InC(SiMe_3)_3]_4$ with o-nitrosotoluene gives a cubic cluster and product D, which contains two benzene rings. Write the SMILES string for aromatic product D and, if necessary, describe its detailed structure in no more than 50 words.
5.4.4 Oxidation of C with 1,2-thiirane gives a trigonal-bipyramidal cluster E. Write the SMILES string for E and, if necessary, describe its detailed structure in no more than 50 words.

5.6 Reaction of $GaI$ with $Li(THF)_3R$ ($R = SiMe(SiMe_3)_2$) in toluene gives the octahedral cluster $G = [GaR]_6$. In contrast, reaction of $GaI$ with $Na(THF)_2R'$ ($R' = Si(t\text{-}Bu)_3$) in toluene forms the octahedral cluster $H = [Ga_6R'_4Bn_2]^{2-}$, where Bn denotes benzyl.
5.6.1 State the source of the benzyl groups in H.
5.6.3 Explain why G is a highly distorted octahedron whereas H is nearly a regular octahedron.

5.8 Electron-rich cluster compounds: When the number of ligands in a cluster is much smaller than the number of metal atoms, its structure approaches that of a bare metal-atom cluster; such species are called electron-rich cluster compounds. A representative example is the metalloid cluster $K = Ga_{84}[N(SiMe_3)_2]_{20}^{4-}$. This cluster contains 84 Ga atoms, 64 of which are “bare.” Its structure has three layers: a central $Ga_2$ dumbbell with a bond length of 235 pm, approaching a $Ga\equiv Ga$ triple bond; a middle $Ga_{32}$ football-shaped tube; and an outer assembly of three $Ga_{10}$ rings surrounded by 20 $N(SiMe_3)_2$ ligands.
Compare K with the fullerene $Sc_2@C_{84}$, and identify which structural units in K correspond to the encapsulated $Sc_2$ and to the $C_{84}$ carbon cage, respectively.

text_images.description: Unlabeled three-dimensional ball-and-stick molecular model. The overall structure is a vertically symmetric multilayer assembly. The upper and lower layers each contain a polyhedron made of dark-blue spheres, approximately 12 in total. A larger central polyhedron is formed by approximately 12 purple spheres, and the outermost framework contains approximately 24 orange-yellow spheres. Spheres of the same color are connected by solid lines of the same color, with radial connections between layers. The drawing represents the layered structure of the metalloid cluster $K = Ga_{84}[N(SiMe_3)_2]_{20}^{4-}$ described in the question.
